summary: Iteration 10 testing: validated Web Bridge endpoint, Network Graph endpoint, NETWORK center tab, and click-satellite-to-memory wiring. Backend 57/57 passing (8 new + 49 regression). Frontend NETWORK tab + Bridge fetch UI works perfectly. CRITICAL: click-satellite-to-memory feature is BROKEN due to missing prop destructure and missing onClickRef declaration in NeuralCore.jsx — clicking the canvas raises 'onClickRef is not defined' runtime error.

ui_bugs.issue: Runtime error 'onClickRef is not defined' fires on EVERY canvas click. The component signature is `const NeuralCore = ({ introspection, embed })` — the `onLatticeNodeClick` prop is NOT destructured, and there is no `onClickRef = useRef()` / sync useEffect anywhere in the file. So `onClickRef.current(...)` at line 292-293 of NeuralCore.jsx throws ReferenceError. Click-satellite-to-memory therefore never opens the MemoryDrawer. Visible to the user as the red 'Uncaught runtime errors:' overlay.

integration_issues.flow: click satellite -> MemoryDrawer opens with NODE id prefilled
integration_issues.issue: Integration broken at NeuralCore.jsx layer. App.js correctly passes `onLatticeNodeClick={handleLatticeNodeClick}` and MemoryDrawer correctly accepts `initialQuery` and syncs to search input on open (verified by reading code), but NeuralCore never invokes the callback because of the ReferenceError above.

action_items: FIX NeuralCore.jsx: (1) destructure `onLatticeNodeClick` from props, (2) add `const onClickRef = useRef(onLatticeNodeClick);` plus a `useEffect(() => { onClickRef.current = onLatticeNodeClick; }, [onLatticeNodeClick]);` so the latest callback is always callable from the imperative three.js click handler. Without this, the entire click-satellite feature is dead and a runtime error fires on every canvas click.
critical_code_review_comments: NeuralCore.jsx references `onClickRef.current` but never declares the ref nor destructures `onLatticeNodeClick` from props. The 'onClickRef pattern' described in the agent-to-agent context was not implemented.
web_bridge.py: `fetch_failed:{e}` leaks the raw exception string into HTTPException detail — fine for debugging but consider trimming or categorising (timeout vs DNS vs connection).

web_bridge.py network_graph aggregator iterates `db.althea_memories.find({tags:'bridge'})` and looks for any tag containing '.' — collides with any unrelated tag containing a dot. Low risk today, but constrain to (tag != 'bridge' and tag != 'web') for safety.
NetworkScreen.jsx: data-testid for host nodes ends up as `network-node-host:example.com` which contains a `:` and `.` — works in CSS attr selectors but is fragile. Consider sanitising.
NetworkScreen.jsx: positions for nodes are recomputed every render with mutating `groupCounts[n.type]++` — works because of strict ordering, but a useMemo over `graph` would be cleaner.

Backend tests file at /app/backend/tests/test_web_bridge_iter10.py is reusable.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: NeuralCore.jsx was supposed to receive `onLatticeNodeClick` and proxy it through an `onClickRef` to keep the three.js click handler synchronised with the latest React prop. The agent-to-agent note in the request says `onClickRef pattern used so latest prop is always available` but the actual code only contains the consumer (line 292-293: `if (hits.length && onClickRef.current) onClickRef.current(...)`) without the producer (the useRef declaration + useEffect sync) or even destructuring the prop from the component signature. REPRO: open the app, switch to NEURAL tab (default), click anywhere on the 3D canvas → red 'Uncaught runtime errors' overlay appears with 'ReferenceError: onClickRef is not defined at HTMLCanvasElement.onCanvasClick'. MITIGATION: in /app/frontend/src/components/NeuralCore.jsx — change `const NeuralCore = ({ introspection, embed }) => {` to `const NeuralCore = ({ introspection, embed, onLatticeNodeClick }) => {` and inside the component add `const onClickRef = useRef(onLatticeNodeClick);` then `useEffect(() => { onClickRef.current = onLatticeNodeClick; }, [onLatticeNodeClick]);` before the main three.js useEffect.
